title: Prompt Versioning Doc
description: How to version prompts so you can roll back, A/B compare, and answer 'why did the model start saying X two weeks ago?'. Prompts live in git, not in a vendor's playground. Each change has an eval delta. The doc structure is light; the discipline is in the workflow — never edit a prompt in production without a paired eval result.

# Prompt Versioning — [Feature]
_Owner: [AIE] · location: `prompts/[feature-name]/`_

## Where prompts live
_Filesystem path. Prompts are .md or .yaml files in git, not in a vendor's playground or a Notion doc._

## File structure per prompt
```
prompts/refund-policy-bot/
├── system.v1.md         # the system prompt
├── examples.v1.jsonl    # few-shot examples if used
├── changelog.md         # what changed when, with eval delta
└── README.md            # what this prompt does + how it's tested
```

## Changelog format
_One entry per change. Each entry: version number, date, what changed (one sentence), eval delta (numbers from before/after), author._

## Branching + review
_Prompt changes go through PR review like any other code change. Required reviewer: at least one other AIE; for customer-facing prompts, also the eng lead. Eval run is required and must show no regression on the critical subset._

## Rollback procedure
_If a prompt change causes a production issue: revert the file, redeploy. The git history is the rollback history. No 'I forgot the previous version' allowed._

worked_examples.content_md:
# Refund-Policy-Bot — Prompt Changelog

## v3 — 14 May 2026 — [AIE]

**What changed:** Added explicit instruction: 'If asked about refund policy, cite the exact policy document by name and quote the relevant paragraph. Do not paraphrase the policy or infer policy from general practices.'

**Eval delta:**
- Critical subset: 9/12 → 12/12 (3 examples now pass that previously hallucinated 30-day policy under leading questions)
- Full set: 28/32 → 31/32 (one example now over-cites; flagged for v4)
- Cost per response: +6% (the citation instruction adds ~80 tokens per response)

**Trigger:** the 14 May customer incident — assistant invented a 30-day refund policy.

## v2 — 4 April 2026 — Tomasz Wójcik (paired with AIE)

**What changed:** Reworded the system prompt to put policy boundaries earlier in the instruction set. Moved 'never invent a policy' instruction from position 8 to position 3.

**Eval delta:**
- Critical subset: 8/12 → 9/12
- Full set: 26/32 → 28/32
- Cost per response: no change

**Note:** This was a structural rewrite based on the observation that instruction position matters for adherence (Anthropic guidance on prompt structure). The v3 update was needed because instruction order alone wasn't enough.

## v1 — 15 March 2026 — Tomasz Wójcik

**What changed:** Initial system prompt. Three sections: role, refund-policy-content, tone guidance.

**Eval delta:** N/A (baseline). 22/32 on full set; 6/12 on critical subset.

**Note:** The 6/12 on critical was acceptable for an MVP but flagged for follow-up; we never got back to it before the 14 May incident, which is the lesson on its own.

annotations.note: Prompts in git, not in a vendor's playground. The team needs to be able to diff, blame, branch, revert. A prompt sitting in a UI somewhere is not versioned in any meaningful sense — it's just the current state.
Changelog with eval delta is the discipline. 'Made the prompt better' is not a changelog entry; '9/12 → 12/12 on critical subset' is.

The v1 entry has a 'note' acknowledging the team accepted 6/12 on critical at MVP — and that the 14 May incident was the consequence of never going back to fix it. The changelog is also a record of decisions and their consequences.

Cost-per-response tracked alongside eval performance. The v3 update was a 6% cost increase for a 3-example improvement on critical evals. Recording the trade-off lets the team have the cost-vs-quality conversation later with data, not opinions.

common_mistakes: Prompts maintained in a vendor playground or Notion. Untrackable, unreviewable, easy to lose. Always in git.
Changelog without eval delta. 'Made it better' isn't auditable. Always show the before/after numbers.
No PR review on prompt changes. Production code changes go through review; prompts are production code. Same standard.
Cost-per-response not tracked. A prompt that doubles in size for a 1% eval improvement may not be worth it; without the cost tracking, you can't have that conversation.
No rollback procedure documented. When a prompt change causes a production issue at 4pm Friday, the team needs to know exactly how to revert without panicking.
Versioning the prompt without versioning the few-shot examples. The few-shot set is part of the prompt; changes to it must be versioned the same way.
variant_patterns: Multi-prompt variant (system + user-context + tool-descriptions): version each piece separately; the runtime composition is also versioned (as a config that names which versions of each piece to use).

Multi-tenant variant (different prompts per customer segment): the changelog tracks which segment(s) a change applies to. Default to no per-tenant prompts; the explosion of variants becomes ungovernable.

Vendor-hosted prompt-management variant (e.g. PromptLayer, LangSmith): the prompts live in the vendor system but you keep a git-mirrored backup. The vendor is convenient but you don't want to lose your prompt history if the vendor changes terms.
